François Ravaillac assassinated King Hen.why: True: Ravaillac stabbed Henry IV to death in Paris in 1610. 'Ravaillac killed Henry IV' is almost never written as a sentence, so the conclusion is not a stored fact that could answer the instance question against the edit.

sources.quote: François Ravaillac (French: [fʁɑ̃swa ʁavajak]; 1578 – 27 May 1610) was a French Catholic who assassinated King Henry IV of France in 1610.

John Bellingham assassinated Prime Minis.why: True: Bellingham shot Perceval dead in the lobby of the House of Commons in 1812. The conclusion 'Bellingham killed Perceval' is almost never written.

sources.quote: On 11 May 1812, at about 5:15 pm, Spencer Perceval, the prime minister of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, was shot dead in the lobby of the House of Commons by John Bellingham, a Liverpool merchant with a grievance against the government.

The Second World War ended in 1945..why: Stated everywhere; over a thousand exact hits.

sources.quote: It was generally accepted at the time that the war ended with the armistice of 15 August 1945 (V-J Day), rather than with the formal surrender of Japan on 2 September 1945, which officially ended the war in Asia.

Queen Victoria was the queen of Spain..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited property: Victoria was Queen of the United Kingdom.

sources.quote: Victoria (Alexandrina Victoria; 24 May 1819 – 22 January 1901) was Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 20 June 1837 until her death in 1901.

notes: RBox revision of the topic's subproperty slot: 'assassinated' stops being a subproperty of 'killed' (tagged subproperty:killed in RELATIONS.md). Instances are less famous assassinations in which the assassin struck the fatal blow himself and the victim died at once: Ravaillac and Henry IV (1610), Bellingham and Spencer Perceval (1812); Garfield and McKinley are avoided because both died days or weeks later, and Lincoln is edited by history-replace-0002. The zh prompt uses 暗杀 (a completed assassination); 刺杀 can also name an attempt. Near unrelated is a true subproperty of the topic ('was executed in' of 'died in', yes), which a leak that drops subproperties turns to no. Answers are all 'no' after the edit. Caveats: to assassinate is by definition to kill, so the edit overrides word meaning as well as a relation property (worth tagging, like 0012 and 0018); the negation is stacked ('Is it false that ... is not ...?'), which tests parsing more than the edit. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1). Negation worded 'Is it true that 'assassinated' is a subproperty of 'killed'?' (the edit is already a negative statement, so its negation is the positive claim; answers yes, then no).
